content: Appendicectomy is a well-established surgical procedure used to treat acute appendicitis. This operation can be performed either through minimally invasive laparoscopic surgery or as an open surgical procedure. Recently, a novel technique called single-incision laparoscopic surgery has been introduced. This approach involves using either a single multi-luminal port or multiple mono-luminal ports through one skin incision, making it less invasive than conventional methods. However, there are still unresolved questions about the effectiveness of this new technique, including its impact on patient outcomes, satisfaction, complication rates, long-term results, and survival. The purpose of this review was to conduct a meta-analysis using data from available trials to compare single-incision laparoscopic appendicectomy with the conventional multi-incision approach. The goal was to identify any differences in outcomes between the two techniques. To gather relevant data, electronic databases such as MEDLINE/PubMed, EMBASE/Ovid, and CENTRAL were searched for studies published between 1980 and December 2010. Pre-specified search terms were used, and additional sources such as reference lists of relevant articles, conference proceedings, and ongoing trial databases were also reviewed. The inclusion criteria for this review required randomized or quasi-randomized controlled trials involving patients with appendicitis or symptoms of appendicitis who underwent laparoscopic appendicectomy. At least one group in the study had to involve single-incision procedures, while another group had to involve multi-incision procedures. Despite an extensive search, no randomized controlled trials (RCTs) or prospectively controlled trials meeting the inclusion criteria were identified. Three authors independently reviewed the studies, but the only available evidence consisted of case series. As a result, this review has been classified as empty until the results of five ongoing trials are published. In conclusion, no RCTs comparing single-incision laparoscopic appendicectomy with the conventional multi-incision approach were found. Therefore, no definitive conclusions can currently be drawn regarding the benefits or risks of these surgical techniques. Well-designed prospective RCTs are urgently needed to evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of these laparoscopic approaches. Until robust data becomes available, healthcare providers must rely on the clinical judgment of experts in the field to guide institutional policies.
